items.label: finalizeRepositoryWitness partial-state atomicity
items.finding: finalizeRepositoryWitness is not atomic: when it throws STOP_WITNESS_UNKNOWN it can leave a partial same-project binding in the executor, so an L7 adjudication evaluated after a caught throw would be ADJUDICATED. The governed protocol does not catch that throw, so the state is unreachable in the certified run path.

items.label: standalone bundle lookup can bind an unadjudicated same-value project
items.finding: The standalone EC-1 bundle lookup binds by VALUE: a project whose link.repo was not adjudicated but equals an adjudicated value can be bound. Affects only the standalone EC-1 CLI, not the in-run executor lookup.

items.label: missing author test for second-team case
items.finding: No author test pins that the S2 team is the request's own pendingScope when more than one team is in scope: reviewer mutant X02 (first team taken instead) is killed only by the reviewer's probe.

items.label: unpinned duplicate-value normative case
items.finding: The duplicate-value / conflicting-binding normative case is not pinned: reviewer mutant X08 (binding-conflict check removed) survives every suite.

items.label: standalone EC-1 exact-equality test gap
items.finding: The standalone EC-1 path has no test pinning exact (case-sensitive) equality: reviewer mutant X15 (case-insensitive bundle lookup) is killed only by the reviewer's probe.

items.label: redundant EC-1 layer mutation masking
items.finding: The EC-1 layers are mutually redundant, so single-layer mutants X23, X24 and X27 mask each other and survive; each layer's independent sufficiency is not shown by single-mutant evidence.

items.label: v1.0.9 section-label erratum
items.finding: Amendment v1.0.9 carries a section-label erratum. The amendment is append-only and is not edited by this record; any correction belongs to a later append-only erratum.

items.label: TypeScript private is compile-time, not runtime #private
items.finding: The executor's same-run binding state is protected by the TypeScript 'private' modifier, which is erased at compile time; it is not an ECMAScript runtime #private field, so in-process code can reach it at runtime.
